source.text: עַל־מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֣י אֶעֱמֹ֔דָה וְאֶֽתְיַצְּבָ֖ה עַל־מָצ֑וֹר וַאֲצַפֶּ֗ה לִרְאוֹת֙ מַה־יְדַבֶּר־בִּ֔י וּמָ֥ה אָשִׁ֖יב עַל־תּוֹכַחְתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: At my watchpost I will stand, and I will station myself on [the] rampart, and I will watch to see what he will speak to me, and what I will answer concerning my complaint.

en.L: At my watchpost I will stand, \q and I will station myself on [the] rampart; \q and I will look out to see what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will speak with me, \q and what I will reply concerning my complaint.
en.B: I will stand at my watchpost \q and take my place on the rampart. \q I will look out to learn what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will say to me, \q and how I should answer about my complaint.
en.R: I will stand guard at my post \q and wait on the city wall. \q I will watch to see what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will say to me, \q and what I should say about my complaint.

fr.L: À mon poste de garde je me tiendrai, \q et je me placerai sur le rempart ; \q et je guetterai pour voir ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me dira, \q et ce que je répondrai au sujet de ma plainte.
fr.B: Je me tiendrai à mon poste de garde \q et je prendrai place sur le rempart. \q Je guetterai pour savoir ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me dira, \q et ce que je devrai répondre au sujet de ma plainte.
fr.R: Je vais monter la garde à mon poste \q et attendre sur la muraille de la ville. \q Je guetterai pour voir ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} va me dire, \q et ce que je devrai dire au sujet de ma plainte.

es.L: En mi puesto de guardia estaré, \q y me apostaré sobre [la] muralla; \q y vigilaré para ver qué me dirá {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, \q y qué responderé acerca de mi queja.
es.B: Me mantendré en mi puesto de guardia \q y ocuparé mi lugar sobre la muralla. \q Vigilaré para saber qué me dirá {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, \q y cómo debo responder acerca de mi queja.
es.R: Me quedaré vigilando en mi puesto \q y esperaré sobre la muralla de la ciudad. \q Estaré atento para ver qué me dirá {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} \q y qué debo decir acerca de mi queja.

decisions.choice: my watchpost ... the rampart: the prophet as a watchman
decisions.reason: A watchman stood on the wall to look out for messengers or danger and report what he saw (2 Samuel 18:24-27; Isaiah 21:6-8). The prophets call themselves watchmen for God's word (Jeremiah 6:17; Ezekiel 3:17). Habakkuk will wait for the LORD's answer as a sentry waits for news; he may also mean a real place of prayer and watching.

decisions.choice: what I will answer concerning my complaint
alternatives: what I will answer when I am corrected
decisions.reason: The word translated "complaint" can also mean "rebuke" or "correction". The line may mean what Habakkuk will say when God answers his complaint, or how he should respond when God corrects him. Either way he expects God to answer.

decisions.choice: the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD as the "he" who will speak.

decisions.choice: "mi puesto de guardia"
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "centinela" for the watchman and uses "puesto de guardia" for the post here; the word stays the same at every level.

source.text: וַיַּעֲנֵ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר כְּת֣וֹב חָז֔וֹן וּבָאֵ֖ר עַל־הַלֻּח֑וֹת לְמַ֥עַן יָר֖וּץ ק֥וֹרֵא בֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered me Yahweh and said: Write [the] vision, and make [it] plain on the tablets, so that may run [one who] reads it.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered me and said: \q Write [the] vision; make [it] plain on the tablets, \q so that one who reads it may run.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered me: \q Write down the vision; make it plain on tablets, \q so that whoever reads it can run.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered me: \q Write down the vision. Make it clear on tablets \q so that whoever reads it can run with the message.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me répondit et dit : \q Écris [la] vision ; grave-[la] clairement sur les tablettes, \q afin que celui qui la lit puisse courir.
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me répondit : \q Écris la vision ; grave-la clairement sur des tablettes, \q pour que celui qui la lit puisse courir.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a répondu : \q Écris la vision. Grave-la bien lisiblement sur des tablettes, \q pour que celui qui la lit puisse courir transmettre le message.

es.L: Y me respondió {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y dijo: \q Escribe [la] visión, y grába[la] con claridad en las tablas, \q para que pueda correr el que la lea.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me respondió: \q Escribe la visión; grábala con claridad en tablas, \q para que quien la lea pueda correr.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me respondió: \q Escribe la visión. Ponla con letras claras en unas tablas \q para que quien la lea pueda correr a llevar el mensaje.

decisions.choice: write the vision ... on the tablets: a public, lasting record
decisions.reason: Tablets were flat pieces of clay, wood or stone used for writing. A message written on tablets could be set up for all to read and kept as a witness that the LORD had said it beforehand (Isaiah 8:1; 30:8). "Make it plain" is used of writing the law clearly on stones in Deuteronomy 27:8.

decisions.choice: so that one who reads it may run
alternatives: so that it can be read at a glance
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean that a messenger who reads it can run to spread it, as prophets are said to "run" with God's word (Jeremiah 23:21), or that it is so plain that a passer-by can read it at a glance. Both readings stress that the message must be clear and spread.

decisions.choice: run with the message
decisions.reason: Readable adds "with the message" to make the running clear, following the first reading of m2; the second is noted there.

decisions.choice: "me répondit" (L, B), "m'a répondu" (R) for the short narrative frame; the LORD's answer takes no quotation marks
decisions.reason: The one line of narration in the book follows the narrative rule (passé simple at L and B); God's answer is an oracle and, as in the English, takes no quotation marks.

decisions.choice: "grábala con claridad" (L, B); "ponla con letras claras" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to make the writing distinct, as on a tablet; Spanish says "grabar con claridad" at L and B and plainer words at R.

decisions.choice: no quotation marks
decisions.reason: God's answer is an oracle, so it takes no quotation marks, as the Spanish prophets set.

source.text: כִּ֣י ע֤וֹד חָזוֹן֙ לַמּוֹעֵ֔ד וְיָפֵ֥חַ לַקֵּ֖ץ וְלֹ֣א יְכַזֵּ֑ב אִם־יִתְמַהְמָהּ֙ חַכֵּה־ל֔וֹ כִּֽי־בֹ֥א יָבֹ֖א לֹ֥א יְאַחֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: For still [the] vision [is] for the appointed time, and it hastens to the end, and not will it lie; if it delays, wait for it; for surely it will come; not will it be late.

en.L: For still [the] vision [is] for the appointed time; \q it hastens to the end, and it will not lie. \q If it delays, wait for it; \q for it will surely come; it will not be late.
en.B: For the vision still waits for its appointed time; \q it hurries toward the end and will not prove false. \q Though it lingers, wait for it; \q it will certainly come and will not be late.
en.R: The vision is for a time that God has set. \q It is hurrying toward the end, and it will not fail. \q If it seems slow in coming, wait for it. \q It will surely come. It will not be late.

fr.L: Car la vision [est] encore pour le temps fixé ; \q elle se hâte vers la fin, et elle ne mentira pas. \q Si elle tarde, attends-la ; \q car elle viendra sûrement ; elle ne sera pas en retard.
fr.B: Car la vision attend encore le moment fixé ; \q elle se hâte vers la fin et ne décevra pas. \q Même si elle se fait attendre, attends-la ; \q elle viendra certainement, elle ne tardera pas.
fr.R: La vision est pour un moment que Dieu a fixé. \q Elle se dépêche vers la fin, et elle ne manquera pas de se réaliser. \q Si elle te semble lente à venir, attends-la. \q Elle viendra sûrement. Elle ne sera pas en retard.

es.L: Porque aún [es] la visión para el tiempo señalado; \q se apresura hacia el fin, y no mentirá. \q Si se retrasa, espérala; \q porque ciertamente vendrá; no tardará.
es.B: Porque la visión aún espera su tiempo señalado; \q se apresura hacia el fin y no resultará falsa. \q Aunque se demore, espérala; \q sin falta vendrá y no se retrasará.
es.R: La visión es para un tiempo que Dios ha fijado. \q Se apresura hacia el fin, y no fallará. \q Si parece que tarda, espérala. \q Vendrá sin falta. No llegará tarde.

decisions.choice: the appointed time ... it hastens to the end
decisions.reason: The vision speaks of a time God has fixed, and of the "end", the time of fulfillment (compare Daniel 8:19; 10:14). The verb may mean "pant" or "hasten" toward it; with a different sense of a word of the same form, it may mean that the vision "testifies" of the end (Proverbs 6:19).

decisions.choice: it will surely come; it will not be late
decisions.reason: "It" is the vision, or what the vision announces. The verb is doubled for certainty: it will come without fail, even if it seems slow. In Hebrew the same words could be read "he will surely come", and the Greek translation read them of a person. Hebrews 10:37 quotes the Greek of this line, "the one who is coming will come and will not delay", before quoting verse 4.

decisions.choice: a time that God has set
decisions.reason: Readable says who appointed the time.

source.text: הִנֵּ֣ה עֻפְּלָ֔ה לֹא־יָשְׁרָ֥ה נַפְשׁ֖וֹ בּ֑וֹ וְצַדִּ֖יק בֶּאֱמוּנָת֥וֹ יִחְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, puffed up, not upright [is] his soul in him; but [the] righteous by his faithfulness will live.

en.L: Look, puffed up, his soul [is] not upright within him; \q but the righteous by {{gender:their|his}} faithfulness will live.
en.B: Look at the proud one: his desires are not upright within him; \q but the righteous will live by {{gender:their|his}} faithfulness.
en.R: Look at the proud enemy. His heart is not right. \q But the person who does right will live by being faithful.

fr.L: Voici, enflée, son âme n’[est] pas droite en lui ; \q mais le juste, par sa fidélité, vivra.
fr.B: Regarde l’orgueilleux : ses désirs ne sont pas droits en lui ; \q mais le juste vivra par sa fidélité.
fr.R: Regarde l’ennemi orgueilleux. Son cœur n’est pas droit. \q Mais celui qui fait ce qui est juste vivra en restant fidèle.

es.L: Mira, el envanecido: no es recta su alma dentro de él; \q pero el justo por su fidelidad vivirá.
es.B: Mira al orgulloso: sus deseos no son rectos dentro de él; \q pero el justo vivirá por su fidelidad.
es.R: Mira al enemigo orgulloso. Su corazón no es recto. \q Pero la persona que hace lo correcto vivirá por ser fiel.

decisions.choice: puffed up, his soul is not upright within him
alternatives: if he draws back, my soul has no pleasure in him (Greek)
decisions.reason: The first line is hard. The verb is used only here and is taken to mean "swollen", that is, proud; "his soul" is his inner self and its desires. The proud one is the arrogant man of verse 5, the Babylonian, set against the righteous. The Greek translation reads the line differently: "if he draws back, my soul has no pleasure in him". Hebrews 10:38 quotes that Greek form after the second line.

decisions.choice: by his faithfulness: by steady loyalty to God, whose faithfulness is meant being uncertain
alternatives: by its faithfulness, the reliability of the vision
decisions.reason: The word (*'emunah*) means firmness, steadiness and trustworthiness: Moses' hands were "steady" (Exodus 17:12), and the word is used of God's own faithfulness (Deuteronomy 32:4; Psalm 89:2). In people it is loyal trust in God that holds firm, and shows itself in a faithful life. Here it is the righteous person's own faithfulness ("his"), in contrast to the pride of the Babylonian: the one who keeps trusting God through the coming disaster will live. The Greek translation reads "my faithfulness", that is, God's faithfulness. Some read "its", the reliability of the vision of verse 3. The Hebrew text has "his".

decisions.choice: Romans 1:17, Galatians 3:11 and Hebrews 10:38 quote this line in Greek, as "the righteous will live by faith"
decisions.reason: Paul quotes the line twice to show that people are put right with God by faith, not by keeping the law (Romans 1:17; Galatians 3:11). Hebrews 10:38 quotes it, in the Greek form "my righteous one will live by faith", to urge believers to keep trusting and not draw back. In each case the Greek word means faith or trust. The Hebrew word stresses the faithfulness that trust produces; both describe a life that rests on God and holds firm in him.

decisions.choice: the righteous: the one who is right with God and does what is right
decisions.reason: In the prophets the righteous person is one who is loyal to God and lives by his ways (Ezekiel 18:5-9). In this book the righteous are those wronged by the wicked (1:4, 13).

decisions.choice: by their faithfulness (L, B); by being faithful (R); not "faith"
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this verse. Literal and Balanced say "faithfulness", not "faith", because the Hebrew word means steady loyalty (m2); the New Testament quotations are translated from their Greek, where the word is "faith" (m3). "The righteous" means any righteous person, man or woman, so the pronoun is a gender span. Readable says "the person who does right" and "by being faithful".

decisions.choice: the proud one (B); the proud enemy (R); desires, heart (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who is "puffed up" (m1). "Soul" here is the inner self; Balanced says "desires" and Readable "heart".

decisions.choice: "sa fidélité" with no gender span, where the English has {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The French possessive "sa" agrees with "fidélité" and says nothing about the sex of the righteous person, so French needs no gender setting here (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: "le juste … vivra" (L, B) as Romans 1:17, but "par sa fidélité", never "par la foi"
decisions.reason: Romans 1:17, Galatians 3:11 and Hebrews 10:38 quote the Greek, "by faith"; the Hebrew *emunah* is steady faithfulness. French keeps the published New Testament's "le juste vivra" so the quotation is seen, and translates the Hebrew noun as "fidélité". Readable says it as a way of living ("en restant fidèle"), as the English Readable.

decisions.choice: "el justo por su fidelidad vivirá" (L); "el justo vivirá por su fidelidad" (B); "la persona que hace lo correcto vivirá por ser fiel" (R)
alternatives: el justo por la fe vivirá
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording. 'Emunah is "fidelidad", not the New Testament's "fe"; "el justo ... vivirá" is kept so that Romans 1:17, Galatians 3:11 and Hebrews 10:38 ("por la fe") can be seen. "Su" covers both sexes, so there is no gender span.

source.text: וְאַף֙ כִּֽי־הַיַּ֣יִן בּוֹגֵ֔ד גֶּ֥בֶר יָהִ֖יר וְלֹ֣א יִנְוֶ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֩ הִרְחִ֨יב כִּשְׁא֜וֹל נַפְשׁ֗וֹ וְה֤וּא כַמָּ֨וֶת֙ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׂבָּ֔ע וַיֶּאֱסֹ֤ף אֵלָיו֙ כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וַיִּקְבֹּ֥ץ אֵלָ֖יו כָּל־הָעַמִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And moreover, the wine is treacherous; an arrogant man, and he will not stay at home, who has made wide like Sheol his throat, and he [is] like death and is not satisfied; and he has gathered to himself all the nations, and he has collected to himself all the peoples.

en.L: And moreover, the wine is treacherous; \q an arrogant man will not stay at rest, \q who makes his throat as wide as Sheol, and he [is] like death and is not satisfied; \q he gathers to himself all the nations \q and collects to himself all the peoples.
en.B: Moreover, wine betrays the arrogant man; \q he is never at rest. \q He opens his throat as wide as Sheol; like death, he is never satisfied. \q He gathers all the nations for himself \q and collects all the peoples as his own.
en.R: Wine deceives the proud man, \q and he never rests. \q His appetite is as big as the grave. Like death, he always wants more. \q He gathers all the nations for himself \q and takes all the peoples as his own.

fr.L: Et de plus, le vin est perfide ; \q l’homme arrogant ne restera pas en repos, \q lui qui élargit sa gorge comme le Shéol, et il [est] comme la mort et n’est pas rassasié ; \q il rassemble vers lui toutes les nations \q et réunit vers lui tous les peuples.
fr.B: De plus, le vin trahit l’homme arrogant ; \q il n’est jamais en repos. \q Il ouvre sa gorge aussi grande que le séjour des morts ; comme la mort, il n’est jamais rassasié. \q Il rassemble pour lui toutes les nations \q et réunit tous les peuples comme son bien.
fr.R: Le vin trompe l’homme orgueilleux, \q et il ne se repose jamais. \q Son appétit est aussi grand que le séjour des morts. Comme la mort, il en veut toujours plus. \q Il rassemble toutes les nations pour lui-même \q et prend tous les peuples comme s’ils lui appartenaient.

es.L: Y además, el vino es traicionero; \q el hombre arrogante no se quedará quieto, \q que ensancha como el Seol su garganta, y él [es] como la muerte y no se sacia; \q reúne para sí a todas las naciones \q y recoge para sí a todos los pueblos.
es.B: Además, el vino traiciona al hombre arrogante; \q nunca está tranquilo. \q Abre su garganta tan ancha como el lugar de los muertos; como la muerte, nunca se sacia. \q Reúne para sí a todas las naciones \q y se apropia de todos los pueblos.
es.R: El vino engaña al hombre orgulloso, \q y nunca descansa. \q Su apetito es tan grande como el sepulcro. Como la muerte, siempre quiere más. \q Reúne para sí a todas las naciones \q y se queda con todos los pueblos.

decisions.choice: the wine is treacherous
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "the wine". Wine makes the proud man reckless and false; the Babylonians were known for their feasting (Daniel 5). The commentary on Habakkuk among the Dead Sea Scrolls reads "wealth", a word that looks much like it, and some prefer that reading. The translation keeps the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: he will not stay at rest
decisions.reason: The verb is rare. It may mean to stay at home, to rest, or to reach one's goal: the arrogant man is never content and always on the move for more conquest.

decisions.choice: his throat as wide as Sheol, like death never satisfied: endless greed
decisions.reason: Sheol, the place of the dead, and death itself are pictured as a mouth that swallows everyone and is never full (Isaiah 5:14; Proverbs 27:20; 30:15-16). The Babylonian swallows nation after nation.

decisions.choice: the grave (R)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, Readable says "the grave" for Sheol, and "appetite" for "throat".

decisions.choice: "el Seol" (L); "el lugar de los muertos" (B); "el sepulcro" (R)
decisions.reason: Sheol follows the Spanish of the Psalms and Isaiah: kept at L, explained at B. R says "sepulcro", as the English R says "the grave".

source.text: הֲלוֹא־אֵ֣לֶּה כֻלָּ֗ם עָלָיו֙ מָשָׁ֣ל יִשָּׂ֔אוּ וּמְלִיצָ֖ה חִיד֣וֹת ל֑וֹ וְיֹאמַ֗ר ה֚וֹי הַמַּרְבֶּ֣ה לֹּא־ל֔וֹ עַד־מָתַ֕י וּמַכְבִּ֥יד עָלָ֖יו עַבְטִֽיט׃

records.literal_gloss: Will not these all of them against him take up a taunt, and a mocking poem, riddles about him, and say: Woe [to the one who] increases what [is] not his! Until when? And [who] makes heavy on himself pledges!

en.L: Will not all of these take up a taunt against him, \q a mocking poem and riddles about him, and say: \q Woe, [the one who] multiplies what is not his own! How long? \q And [who] loads himself with pledges!
en.B: Will not all of them take up a mocking song against him, \q with scorn and riddles about him, and say: \q Woe to him who piles up what is not his own! How long will this go on? \q He weighs himself down with goods taken in pledge!
en.R: All the nations he has conquered will sing songs to make fun of him. \q They will mock him with riddles and say: \q How terrible it will be for the one who takes what does not belong to him! How long can this last? \q He grows rich on what he takes from people who owe him.

fr.L: Ceux-ci, tous, ne lanceront-ils pas contre lui une satire, \q un poème moqueur, des énigmes sur lui, et ne diront-ils pas : \q Malheur, [celui qui] accumule ce qui n’est pas à lui ! Jusqu’à quand ? \q Et [qui] se charge de gages !
fr.B: Tous ne chanteront-ils pas contre lui un chant moqueur, \q avec des railleries et des énigmes sur lui ? Ils diront : \q Malheur à celui qui entasse ce qui ne lui appartient pas ! Jusqu’à quand cela durera-t-il ? \q Il se charge de biens pris en gage !
fr.R: Toutes les nations qu’il a conquises chanteront des chansons pour se moquer de lui. \q Elles se moqueront de lui avec des énigmes et diront : \q Quel malheur pour celui qui prend ce qui n’est pas à lui ! Combien de temps cela peut-il durer ? \q Il s’enrichit avec ce qu’il prend à ceux qui lui doivent de l’argent.

es.L: ¿No alzarán todos estos contra él un refrán de burla, \q un poema satírico y enigmas acerca de él, y dirán: \q ¡Ay del que multiplica lo que no es suyo! ¿Hasta cuándo? \q ¡Y [del que] se carga de prendas!
es.B: ¿No le cantarán todos ellos una canción de burla, \q con escarnio y enigmas acerca de él, y dirán: \q ¡Ay del que amontona lo que no es suyo! ¿Hasta cuándo va a durar esto? \q ¡Se carga de bienes tomados en prenda!
es.R: Todas las naciones que conquistó cantarán canciones para burlarse de él. \q Se burlarán de él con enigmas y dirán: \q ¡Qué terrible será para el que se queda con lo que no le pertenece! ¿Cuánto tiempo puede durar esto? \q Se hace rico con lo que les quita a los que le deben.

decisions.choice: a taunt, a mocking poem, riddles
decisions.reason: The words are forms of wise sayings and poems turned to mockery. Isaiah 14:4 uses the first word for the taunt over the king of Babylon. The nations he has swallowed will sing his downfall.

decisions.choice: Woe: the first of five woes
decisions.reason: The taunt is made of five sayings that begin with "Woe" (verses 6, 9, 12, 15 and 19), each followed by its reason and its punishment. "Woe" is the cry of mourning over the dead, raised over one who is doomed (Nahum 3:1). The five woes are both the nations' taunt and the LORD's word, as verses 13 and 16 show, and no one marks where the taunt ends.

decisions.choice: loads himself with pledges: wealth taken by force, like a ruthless creditor
decisions.reason: A pledge was an item a borrower gave as security for a loan; the law limited what could be taken and required that some things be returned (Deuteronomy 24:6, 10-13). Babylon is pictured as a creditor who has seized the goods of the nations, piling up wealth that is not its own. Verse 7 turns the picture around.

decisions.choice: Woe (L); Woe to (B); How terrible it will be for (R); no quotation marks
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this cry (Isaiah 5:8). The taunt runs through the five woes without a marked end and is also the LORD's own word (m2), so no quotation marks are used; a colon after "say" introduces it.

decisions.choice: goods taken in pledge (B); what he takes from people who owe him (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain the pledges (m3). Readable names the nations as those who sing.

decisions.choice: *hoy* "Malheur, [celui qui] …" (L), "Malheur à celui qui …" (B), "Quel malheur pour celui qui … !" (R), in all five woes (2:6, 9, 12, 15, 19), with no quotation marks
decisions.reason: The prophets' French formula for *hoy*, as Isaiah 5:8-22; the taunt song is set as poetry, without quotation marks, as the English.

decisions.choice: "¡Ay del que ...!" (L, B); "¡Qué terrible será para ...!" (R); no quotation marks
decisions.reason: Hoy follows the Spanish prophets in all five woes of this chapter (2:6, 9, 12, 15, 19). The taunt song is part of the oracle and takes no quotation marks, as in the English.

source.text: הֲל֣וֹא פֶ֗תַע יָק֨וּמוּ֙ נֹשְׁכֶ֔יךָ וְיִקְצ֖וּ מְזַעְזְעֶ֑יךָ וְהָיִ֥יתָ לִמְשִׁסּ֖וֹת לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Will not suddenly arise those who bite you, and wake up those who make you tremble? And you will become plunder for them.

en.L: Will not those who bite you arise suddenly, \q and those who make you tremble wake up? \q And you will become plunder for them.
en.B: Will not your creditors rise up suddenly, \q and those who make you tremble wake up? \q Then you will become their plunder.
en.R: Suddenly the people you owe will come to collect, \q and they will wake up and make you tremble. \q Then they will rob you of everything.

fr.L: Ceux qui te mordent ne se lèveront-ils pas soudain, \q et ceux qui te font trembler ne se réveilleront-ils pas ? \q Et tu deviendras pour eux un butin.
fr.B: Tes créanciers ne se lèveront-ils pas soudain, \q et ceux qui te font trembler ne se réveilleront-ils pas ? \q Alors tu deviendras leur butin.
fr.R: Tout à coup, ceux à qui tu dois de l’argent viendront réclamer leur dû. \q Ils se réveilleront et te feront trembler. \q Alors ils te prendront tout ce que tu as.

es.L: ¿No se levantarán de repente los que te muerden, \q y despertarán los que te hacen temblar? \q Y serás para ellos un botín.
es.B: ¿No se levantarán de repente tus acreedores, \q y despertarán los que te hacen temblar? \q Entonces serás su botín.
es.R: De repente vendrán a cobrar los que te prestaron, \q y despertarán y te harán temblar. \q Entonces te robarán todo.

decisions.choice: those who bite you: your creditors
decisions.reason: The word means "those who bite" and also "those who lend at interest" (the verb is used of charging interest in Deuteronomy 23:20). The play on words turns the picture of verse 6 round: the ruthless creditor will find that he has creditors of his own, who will bite.

decisions.choice: you: the taunt now speaks to him
decisions.reason: The saying moves from "him" to "you", speaking to the Babylonian directly, a shift common in the woe sayings (Isaiah 5:8).

decisions.choice: your creditors (B); the people you owe (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the word (m1), since "biters" does not mean creditors in English. Literal keeps the picture. Readable turns the questions into statements.

source.text: כִּֽיאַתָּ֤ה שַׁלּ֨וֹתָ֙ גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֔ים יְשָׁלּ֖וּךָ כָּל־יֶ֣תֶר עַמִּ֑ים מִדְּמֵ֤י אָדָם֙ וַחֲמַס־אֶ֔רֶץ קִרְיָ֖ה וְכָל־יֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: For you have plundered nations many; they will plunder you, all [the] rest of [the] peoples, because of [the] blood of humankind and [the] violence of [the] land, [the] town and all [who] dwell in it.

en.L: Because you have plundered many nations, \q all the rest of the peoples will plunder you, \q because of [the] blood of humankind and violence [done to the] land, \q [to the] city and all who live in it.
en.B: Since you have looted many nations, \q all the peoples who are left will loot you, \q because of the human blood you shed and the violence against the land, \q against the city and all who live in it.
en.R: You have robbed many nations, \q so the peoples who are left will rob you. \q You killed many people. You were violent to the land, \q to the city and to everyone who lives there.

fr.L: Parce que tu as pillé beaucoup de nations, \q tout le reste des peuples te pillera, \q à cause du sang des humains et de la violence [faite au] pays, \q [à la] ville et à tous ceux qui y habitent.
fr.B: Puisque tu as dépouillé de nombreuses nations, \q tous les peuples qui restent te dépouilleront, \q à cause du sang humain que tu as versé et de la violence faite au pays, \q à la ville et à tous ceux qui y habitent.
fr.R: Tu as volé beaucoup de nations, \q alors les peuples qui restent te voleront. \q Tu as tué beaucoup de gens. Tu as été violent envers le pays, \q envers la ville et envers tous ceux qui y vivent.

es.L: Porque tú has saqueado a muchas naciones, \q todo el resto de los pueblos te saqueará a ti, \q por la sangre de los seres humanos y la violencia [hecha a la] tierra, \q [a la] ciudad y a todos los que habitan en ella.
es.B: Como saqueaste a muchas naciones, \q todos los pueblos que quedan te saquearán a ti, \q por la sangre humana que derramaste y la violencia contra la tierra, \q contra la ciudad y contra todos los que viven en ella.
es.R: Robaste a muchas naciones, \q así que los pueblos que quedan te robarán a ti. \q Mataste a mucha gente. Fuiste violento con la tierra, \q con la ciudad y con todos los que viven allí.

decisions.choice: you have plundered ... they will plunder you: judgment that fits the crime
decisions.reason: The punishment matches the wrong, as in Obadiah 15: "As you have done, it will be done to you". Nahum 2:10 says the same of Assyria. Babylon fell to the Persians in 539 BC.

decisions.choice: the land, the city and all who live in it
alternatives: the land of Judah and the city of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The words may be general, any land and city that Babylon has ravaged, or they may mean Judah and Jerusalem in particular. The same line closes verse 17.

decisions.choice: one wording at each level here and in verse 17
decisions.reason: The second half of this verse is repeated word for word in verse 17, and it is worded the same way there at each level.

decisions.choice: "du sang des humains" (L), no gender span, here and in verse 17
decisions.reason: *adam* here is humankind; French "humains" is already inclusive and the English has no setting here, so French adds none. The same wording returns word for word in verse 17.

decisions.choice: one wording at each level here and in verse 17
decisions.reason: The second half of the verse is repeated word for word in verse 17, and the Spanish keeps the same words at each level in both places.

source.text: ה֗וֹי בֹּצֵ֛עַ בֶּ֥צַע רָ֖ע לְבֵית֑וֹ לָשׂ֤וּם בַּמָּרוֹם֙ קִנּ֔וֹ לְהִנָּצֵ֖ל מִכַּף־רָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe [to one who] gains evil gain for his house, to set on high his nest, to be delivered from [the] palm of evil!

en.L: Woe, [the one who] gains evil gain for his house, \q to set his nest on high, \q to be delivered from the grasp of harm!
en.B: Woe to him who gets wicked profit for his house, \q to set his nest up high, \q to be safe from the grasp of disaster!
en.R: How terrible it will be for the one who gets rich by cheating to make his family great! \q He builds his home up high like a bird's nest, \q so that no trouble can reach him.

fr.L: Malheur, [celui qui] gagne un gain mauvais pour sa maison, \q pour placer son nid en haut, \q pour être délivré de la poigne du malheur !
fr.B: Malheur à celui qui fait un profit malhonnête pour sa maison, \q afin de placer son nid bien haut, \q pour être à l’abri des griffes du malheur !
fr.R: Quel malheur pour celui qui s’enrichit en trichant pour rendre sa famille puissante ! \q Il bâtit sa maison très haut, comme un nid d’oiseau, \q pour que rien de mal ne puisse l’atteindre.

es.L: ¡Ay del que obtiene ganancia injusta para su casa, \q para poner en alto su nido, \q para librarse de la mano del mal!
es.B: ¡Ay del que consigue ganancias perversas para su casa, \q para poner su nido en lo alto, \q para ponerse a salvo de las garras de la desgracia!
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para el que se enriquece con trampas para engrandecer a su familia! \q Construye su casa en lo alto, como un nido, \q para que ningún mal lo alcance.

decisions.choice: evil gain for his house: wealth got by violence, for his household and dynasty
decisions.reason: The phrase means profit made by violence or fraud (Jeremiah 22:17; Ezekiel 22:27). "House" can be a building and also a family or royal line; verses 10-11 use both senses.

decisions.choice: to set his nest on high: to make himself safe from all attack
decisions.reason: An eagle's nest on a cliff is out of reach. Edom is accused of the same pride (Jeremiah 49:16; Obadiah 4), and Babylon built high walls and towers. No height will save him.

decisions.choice: Woe (L); Woe to (B); How terrible it will be for (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording, as in verse 6.

source.text: יָעַ֥צְתָּ בֹּ֖שֶׁת לְבֵיתֶ֑ךָ קְצוֹת־עַמִּ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים וְחוֹטֵ֥א נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: You have planned shame for your house, cutting off peoples many, and sinning [against] your soul.

en.L: You have planned shame for your house, \q cutting off many peoples, and sinning [against] your soul.
en.B: Your schemes have brought shame on your house; \q by cutting off many peoples you have forfeited your own life.
en.R: Your plans have brought shame to your family. \q You destroyed many nations, and so you have lost your own life.

fr.L: Tu as projeté la honte pour ta maison, \q en supprimant beaucoup de peuples, et tu as péché [contre] ton âme.
fr.B: Tes projets ont attiré la honte sur ta maison ; \q en supprimant de nombreux peuples, tu as perdu ta propre vie.
fr.R: Tes plans ont couvert ta famille de honte. \q Tu as détruit beaucoup de nations, et c’est ainsi que tu as perdu ta propre vie.

es.L: Has tramado vergüenza para tu casa, \q exterminando a muchos pueblos, y pecando [contra] tu alma.
es.B: Tus planes han traído vergüenza a tu casa; \q al exterminar a muchos pueblos has perdido tu propia vida.
es.R: Tus planes han avergonzado a tu familia. \q Destruiste muchas naciones, y por eso has perdido tu propia vida.

decisions.choice: sinning against your soul: forfeiting your own life
decisions.reason: To sin against one's soul is to bring about one's own death (Proverbs 8:36; 20:2). The one who cut off many peoples has, by that very act, condemned himself.

decisions.choice: You have planned shame for your house: the opposite of what he intended
decisions.reason: He planned glory for his house and has planned, without meaning to, its shame. The irony is the point of the saying.

decisions.choice: forfeited your own life (B); lost your own life (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m1).

source.text: כִּי־אֶ֖בֶן מִקִּ֣יר תִּזְעָ֑ק וְכָפִ֖יס מֵעֵ֥ץ יַעֲנֶֽנָּה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: For a stone from [the] wall will cry out, and a rafter from [the] woodwork will answer it.

en.L: For [the] stone will cry out from [the] wall, \q and [the] rafter from [the] woodwork will answer it.
en.B: The very stones will cry out from the wall, \q and a beam from the woodwork will answer them.
en.R: The stones in the walls of your house will shout out against you, \q and the wooden beams will answer them.

fr.L: Car la pierre crie depuis le mur, \q et la poutre de la charpente lui répond.
fr.B: Les pierres mêmes crient depuis le mur, \q et une poutre de la charpente leur répond.
fr.R: Les pierres des murs de ta maison vont crier contre toi, \q et les poutres en bois leur répondront.

es.L: Porque [la] piedra clamará desde [el] muro, \q y [la] viga del maderamen le responderá.
es.B: Las mismas piedras gritarán desde el muro, \q y una viga del maderamen les responderá.
es.R: Las piedras de las paredes de tu casa gritarán contra ti, \q y las vigas de madera les responderán.

decisions.choice: the stone will cry out from the wall: the house itself bears witness
decisions.reason: The house built by violence testifies against its builder, as Abel's blood cried out from the ground (Genesis 4:10). Stone and wood call to each other like witnesses in court.

decisions.choice: rafter: a beam of the woodwork
decisions.reason: The word is used only here; it is a beam or rafter, or perhaps a piece of the paneling.

decisions.choice: against you
decisions.reason: Readable says that the stones cry out against the builder (m1).

source.text: ה֛וֹי בֹּנֶ֥ה עִ֖יר בְּדָמִ֑ים וְכוֹנֵ֥ן קִרְיָ֖ה בְּעַוְלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe [to one who] builds a city with blood, and establishes a town with injustice!

en.L: Woe, [the one who] builds a city with bloodshed \q and establishes a town with injustice!
en.B: Woe to him who builds a city with bloodshed \q and founds a town with wrongdoing!
en.R: How terrible it will be for the one who builds a city by killing people \q and builds a town by doing wrong!

fr.L: Malheur, [celui qui] bâtit une ville avec le sang \q et fonde une cité par l’injustice !
fr.B: Malheur à celui qui bâtit une ville dans le sang \q et fonde une cité sur l’injustice !
fr.R: Quel malheur pour celui qui bâtit une ville en tuant des gens \q et construit une cité en faisant le mal !

es.L: ¡Ay del que edifica una ciudad con sangre \q y establece una población con injusticia!
es.B: ¡Ay del que construye una ciudad con derramamiento de sangre \q y funda una población con maldad!
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para el que construye una ciudad matando gente \q y levanta una población haciendo el mal!

decisions.choice: builds a city with bloodshed: the words of Micah 3:10
decisions.reason: Micah accuses Jerusalem's leaders of building "Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustice". Habakkuk uses the same words of Babylon, whose great building works were paid for by plunder and the forced labor of conquered peoples (Jeremiah 22:13 says the same of a king of Judah).

decisions.choice: the Micah 3:10 wording; Woe (L), Woe to (B), How terrible it will be for (R)
decisions.reason: The words shared with Micah 3:10 follow the published wording there at Literal and Balanced. The cry "Woe" follows verse 6.

decisions.choice: "edifica ... con sangre" (L); "construye ... con derramamiento de sangre" (B)
decisions.reason: The line repeats Micah 3:10; Micah is not yet in Spanish, so this wording should be shared with Micah 3:10 when it is drafted.

source.text: הֲל֣וֹא הִנֵּ֔ה מֵאֵ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וְיִֽיגְע֤וּ עַמִּים֙ בְּדֵי־אֵ֔שׁ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים בְּדֵי־רִ֥יק יִעָֽפוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Is it not, look, from Yahweh of hosts, that peoples toil for [the] sufficiency of fire, and nations for [the] sufficiency of nothing grow weary?

en.L: Is it not, look, from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts \q that peoples toil only for fire, \q and nations weary themselves for nothing?
en.B: Has not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies decreed \q that the peoples toil only for the fire \q and the nations wear themselves out for nothing?
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has decided \q that everything the nations work so hard to build will only be burned. \q They wear themselves out for nothing.

fr.L: N’est-ce pas, voici, de la part {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} des armées \q que des peuples se fatiguent seulement pour le feu, \q et que des nations s’épuisent pour le néant ?
fr.B: N’est-ce pas {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées qui a décidé \q que les peuples se fatiguent seulement pour le feu \q et que les nations s’épuisent pour rien ?
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées a décidé \q que tout ce que les nations ont construit avec tant de peine finira brûlé. \q Elles se sont épuisées pour rien.

es.L: ¿No [viene] esto, he aquí, {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: \q que los pueblos se fatigan solo para el fuego, \q y las naciones se cansan para nada?
es.B: ¿No ha decretado {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos \q que los pueblos se fatiguen solo para el fuego \q y que las naciones se agoten para nada?
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos ha decidido \q que todo lo que las naciones construyen con tanto esfuerzo terminará quemado. \q Se agotan para nada.

decisions.choice: peoples toil for fire, nations for nothing: the words of Jeremiah 51:58
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 51:58 uses the same words of Babylon's walls: "peoples toil for nothing, and nations for fire". What the conquered nations were forced to build for Babylon will be burned; their labor was in vain. Habakkuk sets the two halves in the other order.

decisions.choice: from the LORD of hosts: it is God who decrees Babylon's end
decisions.reason: The woe of verse 12 is not only the nations' taunt: the LORD himself has decided that the empire built by violence will come to nothing.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts (L); the LORD of Armies (B, R); only for fire, for nothing
decisions.reason: The settled wording for the title. "For the sufficiency of fire" means only to feed the fire; the words follow Jeremiah 51:58 at Balanced ("only for the fire", "wear themselves out").

decisions.choice: "se fatiguent … pour le feu", "s'épuisent pour le néant / pour rien", the published Jeremiah 51:58 words; "le SEIGNEUR des armées" at every level
alternatives: "le SEIGNEUR des Armées" at B and R, as the English "of Armies"
decisions.reason: The line repeats Jeremiah 51:58, so French reuses the published Jeremiah's verbs where the Hebrew is the same. French keeps "le SEIGNEUR des armées" at every level, as the term sheet, where the English Balanced and Readable say "of Armies".

decisions.choice: "los pueblos se fatigan ... para el fuego", "se cansan" / "se agotan para nada"
decisions.reason: The line takes up Jeremiah 51:58, and the Spanish uses that verse's words ("se fatigan", "se agotan", "para el fuego", "para nada") in Habakkuk's order. The LORD of hosts is "de los ejércitos" at L and "de los Ejércitos" at B and R, as in the Spanish prophets.

source.text: כִּ֚י תִּמָּלֵ֣א הָאָ֔רֶץ לָדַ֖עַת אֶת־כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֑ה כַּמַּ֖יִם יְכַסּ֥וּ עַל־יָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For will be filled the earth to know the glory of Yahweh, as the waters cover over [the] sea.

en.L: For the earth will be filled with knowing the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q as the waters cover over the sea.
en.B: For the earth will be as full of knowing the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q as the sea is full of water.
en.R: Everyone on earth will know the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q The earth will be full of this knowledge, just as the oceans are full of water.

fr.L: Car la terre sera remplie de la connaissance de la gloire {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q comme les eaux couvrent la mer.
fr.B: Car la terre sera aussi pleine de la connaissance de la gloire {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} \q que la mer est pleine d’eau.
fr.R: Tout le monde sur la terre connaîtra la gloire {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. \q La terre sera remplie de cette connaissance, comme les océans sont remplis d’eau.

es.L: Porque la tierra será llena del conocimiento de la gloria {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, \q como las aguas cubren el mar.
es.B: Porque la tierra estará tan llena del conocimiento de la gloria {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} \q como el mar está lleno de agua.
es.R: Todos en la tierra conocerán la gloria {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. \q La tierra estará llena de este conocimiento, así como los océanos están llenos de agua.

decisions.choice: the earth filled with the knowledge of the LORD: the words of Isaiah 11:9
decisions.reason: Isaiah 11:9 says: "the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea". Habakkuk adds "the glory of" and says "will be filled". Set among the woes, the line says that Babylon's empire will vanish, but the knowledge of the LORD's glory will cover the earth. Numbers 14:21 and Psalm 72:19 speak of the earth filled with his glory.

decisions.choice: knowing the glory of the LORD: recognizing his greatness and presence
decisions.reason: The glory (*kavod*) of the LORD is his weight, majesty and visible presence. "To know" it is to recognize and acknowledge it, not only to know facts about it.

decisions.choice: the Isaiah 11:9 wording at each level, with "the glory of" added
decisions.reason: Each level reuses the published wording of Isaiah 11:9 ("as the waters cover the sea" at Literal, "as the sea is full of water" at Balanced, "just as the oceans are full of water" at Readable), adding "the glory of" as Habakkuk does. Literal says "filled with knowing", since the Hebrew uses the verb "to know" where Isaiah has the noun, and "cover over" for Habakkuk's "over the sea".

decisions.choice: The published Isaiah 11:9 wording at each level, with "de la gloire" added
decisions.reason: Habakkuk repeats Isaiah 11:9 and adds "the glory of"; French keeps Isaiah's sentence at each level and changes only what the Hebrew changes.

decisions.choice: the Spanish Isaiah 11:9 wording at each level, with "de la gloria" added
decisions.reason: Habakkuk repeats Isaiah 11:9 with "the glory of" added; the Spanish reuses its Isaiah 11:9 lines at each level and adds only those words.

source.text: ה֚וֹי מַשְׁקֵ֣ה רֵעֵ֔הוּ מְסַפֵּ֥חַ חֲמָתְךָ֖ וְאַ֣ף שַׁכֵּ֑ר לְמַ֥עַן הַבִּ֖יט עַל־מְעוֹרֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe [to one who] makes drink his neighbor, mixing in your wrath, and even making [them] drunk, in order to look on their nakedness!

en.L: Woe, [the one who] makes his neighbor drink, \q mixing in your wrath and making [them] drunk, \q in order to look on their nakedness!
en.B: Woe to him who makes his neighbors drink, \q pouring out his fury until they are drunk, \q so that he can gaze at their nakedness!
en.R: How terrible it will be for the one who makes his neighbors drunk, \q pouring out wine mixed with his anger, \q so that he can look at their naked bodies!

fr.L: Malheur, [celui qui] fait boire son prochain, \q en y mêlant ta fureur, et même [l’]enivre, \q afin de regarder leur nudité !
fr.B: Malheur à celui qui fait boire ses voisins, \q en déversant sa fureur jusqu’à les enivrer, \q pour contempler leur nudité !
fr.R: Quel malheur pour celui qui fait boire ses voisins jusqu’à les rendre ivres, \q en leur versant du vin mêlé de sa colère, \q pour pouvoir regarder leur corps nu !

es.L: ¡Ay del que da de beber a su prójimo, \q mezclando tu furor, y aun emborracha[ndolos], \q para mirar su desnudez!
es.B: ¡Ay del que hace beber a sus vecinos, \q derramando su furor hasta emborracharlos, \q para contemplar su desnudez!
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para el que emborracha a sus vecinos, \q dándoles vino mezclado con su enojo, \q para mirarles el cuerpo desnudo!

decisions.choice: makes his neighbor drink ... to look on their nakedness: the shaming of the nations
decisions.reason: The picture is of a host who gets his guests drunk to see them shamefully exposed (compare Genesis 9:21-22). It stands for the way Babylon made the nations drink its wine (Jeremiah 51:7) and stripped them of honor and goods. The next verse turns the cup on Babylon.

decisions.choice: mixing in your wrath
decisions.reason: The word translated "wrath" also means "poison" or "venom" (Deuteronomy 32:24, 33), and the verb may mean "pouring out" or "mixing in". The line may be "mixing in your poison": a drugged drink. "Your" is a sudden shift to speaking to him.

decisions.choice: Woe (L), Woe to (B), How terrible it will be for (R); his neighbors, his fury (B, R)
decisions.reason: The cry follows verse 6. Balanced and Readable say "his" for "your" so that the verse speaks about him throughout; the Hebrew shifts to "your" (m2). "Neighbor" stands for the neighboring nations, so they say "neighbors".

source.text: שָׂבַ֤עְתָּ קָלוֹן֙ מִכָּב֔וֹד שְׁתֵ֥ה גַם־אַ֖תָּה וְהֵֽעָרֵ֑ל תִּסּ֣וֹב עָלֶ֗יךָ כּ֚וֹס יְמִ֣ין יְהוָ֔ה וְקִיקָל֖וֹן עַל־כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: You are sated [with] shame more than glory. Drink, also you, and be exposed as uncircumcised! It will come round to you, the cup of [the] right hand of Yahweh, and utter disgrace [will be] on your glory.

en.L: You are sated with shame instead of glory; \q drink, you too, and be exposed as uncircumcised! \q The cup of the right hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will come around to you, \q and utter disgrace [will be] on your glory.
en.B: You will be filled with shame instead of glory. \q Drink, you too, and be exposed as uncircumcised! \q The cup in the right hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will come around to you, \q and disgrace will cover your glory.
en.R: You will be covered with shame instead of honor. \q Now it is your turn to drink and be shown naked and disgraced! \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} holds a cup of punishment in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand, and it will be passed to you. \q Your glory will turn into shame.

fr.L: Tu es rassasié de honte plutôt que de gloire ; \q bois, toi aussi, et montre-toi incirconcis ! \q La coupe de la main droite {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} viendra jusqu’à toi, \q et l’infamie [sera] sur ta gloire.
fr.B: Tu seras rassasié de honte au lieu de gloire. \q Bois, toi aussi, et montre que tu es incirconcis ! \q La coupe que tient la main droite {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} passera jusqu’à toi, \q et l’infamie couvrira ta gloire.
fr.R: Tu seras couvert de honte au lieu d’honneur. \q Maintenant c’est ton tour de boire et d’être exposé tout nu, couvert de honte ! \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} tient dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main droite une coupe de punition, et elle va passer jusqu’à toi. \q Ta gloire va se changer en honte.

es.L: Te has saciado de vergüenza en vez de gloria; \q ¡bebe tú también, y muestra que eres incircunciso! \q Te llegará a ti la copa de la diestra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, \q y deshonra total [caerá] sobre tu gloria.
es.B: Te llenarás de vergüenza en vez de gloria. \q ¡Bebe tú también, y queda expuesto como incircunciso! \q La copa que está en la mano derecha {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} pasará a ti, \q y la deshonra cubrirá tu gloria.
es.R: Te cubrirás de vergüenza en vez de honra. \q ¡Ahora te toca a ti beber y quedar desnudo y humillado! \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tiene en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano derecha una copa de castigo, y te la pasarán a ti. \q Tu gloria se convertirá en vergüenza.

decisions.choice: be exposed as uncircumcised
alternatives: drink, you too, and stagger (Qumran commentary, Greek)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb means "show your foreskin", that is, be stripped naked and shown to be uncircumcised, a deep shame in Israel's eyes. The commentary on Habakkuk among the Dead Sea Scrolls and the Greek translation read a verb with two letters reversed, "stagger", which fits the picture of drunkenness. The translation keeps the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: the cup of the LORD's right hand: God's judgment, passed round to Babylon
decisions.reason: The prophets picture judgment as a cup of wine that God gives the nations to drink until they stagger (Jeremiah 25:15-29; Psalm 75:9; Isaiah 51:17). It "comes round" like the cup passed from guest to guest at a feast: Babylon made others drink, and now its turn has come (Jeremiah 25:26).

decisions.choice: utter disgrace
decisions.reason: The word is used only here. It seems to be a strengthened form of the word for "shame" in the first line; some see in it the word for vomit, "shameful vomit", fitting the drunken scene.

decisions.choice: You will be filled (B, R); be shown naked and disgraced (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is in the past tense, as often in prophecy, where a coming event is described as done; Balanced and Readable say "will". Readable says what being exposed as uncircumcised means (m1) and explains the cup (m2).

source.text: כִּ֣י חֲמַ֤ס לְבָנוֹן֙ יְכַסֶּ֔ךָּ וְשֹׁ֥ד בְּהֵמ֖וֹת יְחִיתַ֑ן מִדְּמֵ֤י אָדָם֙ וַחֲמַס־אֶ֔רֶץ קִרְיָ֖ה וְכָל־יֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For [the] violence of Lebanon will cover you, and [the] destruction of beasts [that] terrified them, because of [the] blood of humankind and [the] violence of [the] land, [the] town and all [who] dwell in it.

en.L: For [the] violence [done to] Lebanon will cover you, \q and [the] destruction of [the] beasts [that] terrified them, \q because of [the] blood of humankind and violence [done to the] land, \q [to the] city and all who live in it.
en.B: The violence you did to Lebanon will overwhelm you, \q and so will the slaughter that terrified its animals, \q because of the human blood you shed and the violence against the land, \q against the city and all who live in it.
en.R: You cut down the forests of Lebanon and killed its animals. Now that violence will come back on you. \q The slaughter of the animals that terrified them will bury you. \q You killed many people. You were violent to the land, \q to the city and to everyone who lives there.

fr.L: Car la violence [faite au] Liban te couvrira, \q et la destruction des bêtes [qui] les terrifiait, \q à cause du sang des humains et de la violence [faite au] pays, \q [à la] ville et à tous ceux qui y habitent.
fr.B: La violence que tu as faite au Liban t’accablera, \q ainsi que le massacre qui a terrifié ses bêtes, \q à cause du sang humain que tu as versé et de la violence faite au pays, \q à la ville et à tous ceux qui y habitent.
fr.R: Tu as abattu les forêts du Liban et tué ses animaux. Maintenant cette violence va retomber sur toi. \q Le massacre des animaux qui les a terrifiés va t’écraser. \q Tu as tué beaucoup de gens. Tu as été violent envers le pays, \q envers la ville et envers tous ceux qui y vivent.

es.L: Porque [la] violencia [hecha al] Líbano te cubrirá, \q y [la] destrucción de [las] bestias [que] las aterrorizó, \q por la sangre de los seres humanos y la violencia [hecha a la] tierra, \q [a la] ciudad y a todos los que habitan en ella.
es.B: La violencia que le hiciste al Líbano caerá sobre ti, \q y también la matanza que aterrorizó a sus animales, \q por la sangre humana que derramaste y la violencia contra la tierra, \q contra la ciudad y contra todos los que viven en ella.
es.R: Talaste los bosques del Líbano y mataste a sus animales. Ahora esa violencia caerá sobre ti. \q La matanza de los animales que los aterrorizó te sepultará. \q Mataste a mucha gente. Fuiste violento con la tierra, \q con la ciudad y con todos los que viven allí.

decisions.choice: the violence done to Lebanon: the stripping of its forests
alternatives: Lebanon stands for Israel or the temple
decisions.reason: Conquerors felled the cedars of Lebanon for their buildings and hunted its animals (Isaiah 14:8; 37:24). The Babylonian kings, like the Assyrians before them, took timber from Lebanon. Some take Lebanon here as a picture of Israel or the temple, built of its cedar (Jeremiah 22:6, 23).

decisions.choice: the destruction of the beasts that terrified them
alternatives: the destruction of the beasts will terrify you (Greek)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "terrified them", most likely the destruction that terrified the animals. The Greek translation and others read "will terrify you", which matches "will cover you" in the first line. The translation keeps the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: the second half repeats verse 8
decisions.reason: The line "because of human blood and violence to the land, to the city and all who live in it" closes the first woe in verse 8 and is repeated here. See the note there on its meaning.

decisions.choice: the verse 8 wording repeated at each level; violence you did to Lebanon (B); You cut down the forests (R)
decisions.reason: The repeated line keeps the wording of verse 8. Balanced says whose the violence was; Readable says what it was (m1).

source.text: מָֽה־הוֹעִ֣יל פֶּ֗סֶל כִּ֤י פְסָלוֹ֙ יֹֽצְר֔וֹ מַסֵּכָ֖ה וּמ֣וֹרֶה שָּׁ֑קֶר כִּ֣י בָטַ֞ח יֹצֵ֤ר יִצְרוֹ֙ עָלָ֔יו לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת אֱלִילִ֥ים אִלְּמִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: What does profit a carved image, that has carved it its maker, a cast image, and a teacher of falsehood? For trusts [the] maker of its form in it, to make idols mute.

en.L: What does a carved image profit, that its maker has carved it, \q a cast image and a teacher of lies? \q For the one who formed it trusts in his own creation \q when he makes mute idols.
en.B: What use is an idol once its maker has carved it, \q or a metal image, a teacher of lies? \q Its maker trusts in what he himself has shaped \q when he fashions idols that cannot speak.
en.R: What good is an idol that someone has carved, \q or a metal statue? It teaches only lies. \q People who make idols trust in what they have made, \q but their idols cannot even talk.

fr.L: À quoi sert une image taillée, que son fabricant l’ait taillée, \q une image fondue et un maître de mensonge ? \q Car celui qui l’a formée se confie en sa propre œuvre \q quand il fait des idoles muettes.
fr.B: À quoi sert une idole, une fois que l’artisan l’a sculptée, \q ou une statue de métal, un maître de mensonge ? \q Celui qui l’a façonnée met sa confiance dans ce qu’il a fait lui-même \q quand il fabrique des idoles qui ne parlent pas.
fr.R: À quoi sert une idole que quelqu’un a sculptée, \q ou une statue de métal ? Elle n’enseigne que des mensonges. \q Ceux qui fabriquent des idoles ont confiance dans ce qu’ils ont fait, \q mais leurs idoles ne savent même pas parler.

es.L: ¿De qué sirve la imagen tallada, que la ha tallado su hacedor, \q la imagen fundida y maestra de mentira? \q Porque el que la formó confía en su propia obra \q cuando hace ídolos mudos.
es.B: ¿De qué sirve un ídolo una vez que su artesano lo ha tallado, \q o una imagen de metal, maestra de mentiras? \q Su artesano confía en lo que él mismo ha formado \q cuando fabrica ídolos que no pueden hablar.
es.R: ¿De qué sirve un ídolo que alguien ha tallado, \q o una estatua de metal? Solo enseña mentiras. \q Los que hacen ídolos confían en lo que ellos mismos hicieron, \q pero sus ídolos ni siquiera pueden hablar.

decisions.choice: What does a carved image profit?: the folly of idols
decisions.reason: The prophets mock idols as things made by human hands that cannot save (Isaiah 44:9-20; Jeremiah 10:1-16; Psalm 115:4-8). The Babylonian who makes his strength his god (1:11, 16) trusts in what he himself has made.

decisions.choice: a teacher of lies ... mute idols
decisions.reason: Idols were consulted for guidance through their priests, so they are "teachers", but they teach only falsehood. The Hebrew words for "idols" and "mute" sound alike; the first means "worthless things" or "nothings" (Isaiah 2:8).

decisions.choice: People who make idols ... they (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew singular, the craftsman who carves the idol. Readable uses the plural, since he stands for anyone who makes idols, so that no gender span is needed.

source.text: ה֣וֹי אֹמֵ֤ר לָעֵץ֙ הָקִ֔יצָה ע֖וּרִי לְאֶ֣בֶן דּוּמָ֑ם ה֣וּא יוֹרֶ֔ה הִנֵּה־ה֗וּא תָּפוּשׂ֙ זָהָ֣ב וָכֶ֔סֶף וְכָל־ר֖וּחַ אֵ֥ין בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe [to one who] says to wood, Wake up! Awake! to stone of silence. Will it teach? Look, it [is] overlaid [with] gold and silver, and any breath there is not within it.

en.L: Woe, [the one who] says to wood, "Wake up!" \q "Awake!" to silent stone. \q Will it teach? \q Look, it [is] encased in gold and silver, \q and there is no breath at all inside it.
en.B: Woe to him who says to a piece of wood, "Wake up!" \q or to a lifeless stone, "Get up!" \q Can it teach? \q It is covered with gold and silver, \q but there is no breath in it at all.
en.R: How terrible it will be for anyone who says to a piece of wood, "Wake up!" \q or says to a stone that cannot speak, "Get up!" \q Can an idol teach anyone anything? \q It may be covered with gold and silver, \q but it has no life in it at all.

fr.L: Malheur, [celui qui] dit au bois : « Réveille-toi ! » \q « Éveille-toi ! » à la pierre muette. \q Elle, enseigner ? \q Voici, elle [est] plaquée d’or et d’argent, \q et il n’y a aucun souffle au-dedans d’elle.
fr.B: Malheur à celui qui dit à un morceau de bois : « Réveille-toi ! » \q ou à une pierre sans vie : « Lève-toi ! » \q Peut-elle enseigner ? \q Elle est recouverte d’or et d’argent, \q mais il n’y a en elle aucun souffle.
fr.R: Quel malheur pour celui qui dit à un morceau de bois : « Réveille-toi ! » \q ou à une pierre qui ne peut pas parler : « Lève-toi ! » \q Une idole peut-elle enseigner quoi que ce soit ? \q Elle est peut-être couverte d’or et d’argent, \q mais il n’y a aucune vie en elle.

es.L: ¡Ay del que dice al palo: «¡Despierta!», \q «¡Levántate!», a la piedra muda! \q ¿Enseñará ella? \q He aquí, está recubierta de oro y plata, \q y no hay en ella aliento alguno.
es.B: ¡Ay del que le dice a un trozo de madera: «¡Despierta!», \q o a una piedra sin vida: «¡Levántate!»! \q ¿Puede eso enseñar? \q Está recubierto de oro y plata, \q pero no tiene aliento alguno.
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para el que le dice a un trozo de madera: «¡Despierta!», \q o le dice a una piedra que no puede hablar: «¡Levántate!»! \q ¿Puede un ídolo enseñarle algo a alguien? \q Puede estar cubierto de oro y plata, \q pero no tiene nada de vida.

decisions.choice: Wake up! to wood and stone: calling on idols
decisions.reason: Worshipers called on their gods to wake and act, as the prophets of Baal did when Elijah mocked them (1 Kings 18:27). Psalm 44:24 calls on the LORD to "wake up", but the LORD hears; the wood and stone cannot.

decisions.choice: no breath at all within it
decisions.reason: "Breath" is the breath of life (Genesis 2:7). However richly it is plated, the idol is dead (Jeremiah 10:14). The next verse sets the living LORD against it.

decisions.choice: Woe (L); Woe to (B); How terrible it will be for (R)
decisions.reason: The fifth woe follows the wording of verse 6. Readable says "anyone", since the saying applies to every idol worshiper.

source.text: וַֽיהוָ֖ה בְּהֵיכַ֣ל קָדְשׁ֑וֹ הַ֥ס מִפָּנָ֖יו כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: But Yahweh [is] in [the] temple of his holiness; hush before him, all the earth!

en.L: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy temple; \q hush before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, all the earth!
en.B: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy temple; \q all the earth, be hushed before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy temple. \q Everyone on earth should be silent in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence.

fr.L: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [est] dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} saint temple ; \q silence devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, toute la terre !
fr.B: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} saint temple ; \q que toute la terre fasse silence devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} !
fr.R: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} temple saint. \q Que tous les habitants de la terre se taisent devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

es.L: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [está] en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santo templo; \q ¡calle delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} toda la tierra!
es.B: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santo templo; \q ¡que toda la tierra guarde silencio delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}!
es.R: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santo templo. \q Todos en la tierra deben guardar silencio en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} presencia.

decisions.choice: the LORD is in his holy temple: the words of Psalm 11:4
decisions.reason: Psalm 11:4 begins: "The LORD is in his holy temple; the LORD's throne is in heaven." The temple may be the temple in Jerusalem or his dwelling in heaven; the point is that the living God reigns, unlike the lifeless idols of verses 18-19.

decisions.choice: hush before him, all the earth!: silent awe before God who is about to act
decisions.reason: The word is a call for silence, like "Hush!" (Amos 6:10). It is used before the LORD comes to judge (Zephaniah 1:7; Zechariah 2:17). The whole earth, the nations that Babylon ruled and Babylon itself, must fall silent before him. The prayer of chapter 3 follows.

decisions.choice: the Psalm 11:4 wording; hush (L, B); be silent (R)
decisions.reason: "The LORD [is] in his holy temple" follows Psalm 11:4 at each level. Literal and Balanced keep the word "hush"; Readable says "be silent".

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR [est] dans son saint temple" (L), "… est dans son saint temple" (B), "… dans son temple saint" (R), the published Psalm 11:4
decisions.reason: The line is Psalm 11:4; French reuses the published Psalm at each level.

decisions.choice: "está en su santo templo"
decisions.reason: The first line reuses the Spanish of Psalm 11:4 at each level.
